title: Asset Liability Management obligations are tradeable between Primes, separating who allocates from who manages liabilities
content:
A.2.2.10.3 defines the Asset Liability Management Rental Primitive as "a mechanism enabling Prime Agents to trade Asset Liability Management obligations between each other, providing more flexibility in how capital is deployed through the Allocation System and reducing duplicate work." A.2.2.10.2 gives the parallel construct for capital: the Risk Capital Rental Primitive lets Primes "rapidly rent Risk Capital from each other, ensuring that capital gets deployed to where the best opportunities are."

Together these unbundle what would normally be one role. Finding a yield opportunity, underwriting it with loss-absorbing capital, and managing the asset-liability profile that supports it become three functions that can sit with three different Primes. A.2.2.10.1.1.2.1.3.3 already anticipates this at plan time: a Prime's ALM Strategy must state whether it will meet requirements "through its own direct asset management or by transferring its obligations to another Prime Agent via the ASC Rental Primitive," and if the latter, reference the governing Ecosystem Accord.

"Reducing duplicate work" is the second, less obvious motive. ALM is infrastructure — liquidity laddering, redemption readiness, hedging — with real fixed costs and strong returns to scale. Requiring every Prime to build it independently would tax specialisation, especially for a small Prime with one good opportunity.

The structural cost is a web of inter-Prime dependencies: a Prime's compliance can now hinge on another Prime performing an obligation it took on. That is why these arrangements must be codified as Ecosystem Accords in the Atlas and verified by Core GovOps against it, rather than existing as private agreements.
description: The ALM Rental Primitive lets Primes trade ALM obligations to add flexibility in capital deployment and reduce duplicate work, mirroring the Risk Capital Rental Primitive's market for capacity.
